title: Lemon Pepper Chicken Pesto Linguine
summary: A lightened basil pesto (ice water and Greek yogurt standing in for most of the oil) tossed with linguine and seared lemon pepper chicken. The lemon in both the pesto and the seasoning ties the dish together. Makes ~5 servings.

nutrition.label: Traditional (regular pesto, chicken seared in butter)

ingredients.raw: 60g fresh basil leaves, packed and completely dry (thawed from freezer, if using frozen)
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil — adjust down based on oil retained from freezing (see note)
3 tbsp plain Greek yogurt, full-fat preferred
1 tbsp olive oil (for searing the chicken)

steps.body: Coat the chicken with lemon pepper seasoning and a pinch of salt. Let it sit at room temp while you start the pesto.
Measure out the parmesan, garlic, lemon juice, Greek yogurt, and ice water for the pesto.
Get a big pot of salted water going for the linguine first — it takes the longest to come up to a boil.
**Toast the walnuts.** Dry pan, medium heat, 2–3 min, shaking often, until fragrant. Let cool slightly.
**Combine the pesto solids first.** Cooled walnuts, garlic, parmesan, salt, and pepper into the food processor before the basil — this abrasive base helps everything break down evenly.

**Pulse in the basil.** Add basil on top. Pulse 8–10 times in short, sharp bursts — do not run continuously, since friction heats the basil and dulls its color. If the bowl feels warm, stop and let it rest 60 seconds.
**Stream in oil and lemon.** With the processor running, drizzle in the olive oil, then add lemon juice, scraping down the sides.
**Drip in the ice water.** Processor still running, add the ice water about a tablespoon at a time until the sauce visibly thins and brightens — stop while it still has a little bite from the nuts.
**Fold in the yogurt** by hand, off the processor, until creamy. Set the pesto aside.
**Sear the chicken.** Olive oil in a hot pan, chicken in for 6–7 min per side depending on thickness, until it hits 165°F internal. Rest 5 min, then slice.
Once the water's at a hard boil, cook the linguine, pulling it 1–2 min under box time so it's al dente. Reserve pasta water.
**Combine off-heat.** Toss the hot pasta with the pesto, loosening with a splash of pasta water until it coats evenly. Top with sliced chicken and a squeeze of fresh lemon.

notes.body: Freezing basil for this recipe: coat trimmed basil lightly in oil before freezing for best color and quality — a blanch-and-shock (2–3 sec in boiling water, then straight into ice water, patted fully dry) helps it stay bright. Keep a running tally of oil used across all your freezing batches. When it's time to make the pesto, take half that total and subtract it from the 2 tbsp fresh oil above — skip the fresh oil entirely if the retained amount already covers it.
**Solids before basil, basil in short pulses** — continuous blending heats and browns the basil
**Full-fat Greek yogurt blends smoothest.** Low-fat works but is more watery — add gradually
**Fold yogurt in by hand, off the processor** — never blend it in
**Don't overcook the chicken** — pull it right at 165°F and rest before slicing; lemon pepper chicken dries out fast since there's no fat cushion like a marinade would give
**Toss the pasta off-heat** — direct heat on the yogurt-based pesto can cause it to split
Reserve pasta water before draining — you'll need it to loosen the sauce
**Sauce too thick:** more pasta water or ice water, a teaspoon at a time
**Chicken dry:** slice thinner next time and rest longer before cutting; a squeeze of lemon at the end helps mask it
**Grainy sauce:** yogurt was overblended — fold more gently next time
**Dull pesto color:** processor ran too hot — pulse in shorter bursts, let the bowl rest between batches
